headline: Crude +4.4% is the last thing a 5.28% ten-year needed: an oil tax lands with breadth already at a 52-week low.
summary: The new variable today is crude. WTI +4.4% to 92.16, Brent +4.4% to 104.59 — Brent is now $12.4 over WTI, +37.1% in three months and +71.9% year-to-date, with oil/gold +4.1% on the day and +27.5% on three months. Breakevens refused to confirm: 5-year 2.37% and 10-year 2.36%, both flat on the day, both with negative acceleration (-0.61, -0.54). RBOB actually fell 1.6% against crude +4.4%. That combination says supply event and crack compression, not a reflation. It is a tax on margins and the consumer, and it does not buy you a single cut.

The rates damage from yesterday has not healed, and the front-end relief is narrower than it looked. The 30-year added 3bp to 5.67% — the 100th percentile of 52 weeks, acceleration z=1.08. The 10-year is 5.28% at the 97.8th, the 10-year real yield 2.92% with z=1.92 and acceleration 1.38, sitting 36% above its 200-day. The 30-year mortgage is 7.28%, +62bp on the month, also 100th percentile. Yes, the 2-year fell 11bp on the week to 4.77%, but the 3-month bill is +31bp on the month to 4.22% with acceleration 1.06 — the easing is in the 2-year, not in cash. 2s10s at 51bp, +10bp on the month, is term-premium steepening. Rates composite stuck at -80.

What changed versus yesterday: the selling went global and the dollar re-accelerated, while the rot migrated from the mine and the factory to the balance sheet. On today's tape KOSPI -2.6%, Nikkei -1.4%, Hang Seng -1.4%, Euro Stoxx -1.0%, Sensex -1.4% — US cash is still marked at Monday's close. DXY 102.4 at the 100th percentile with acceleration 1.66; EURUSD 1.1186 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks; USDCAD z=1.93/acc 1.84, USDMXN z=2.39/acc 1.90, USDINR z=1.79/acc 1.75. And financials are now the worst large complex on the board: XLF -7.2% on the month (z=-1.66), KBE -8.8%, KRE -8.0%, GS -14.6% (z=-2.08), BX -17.9%, IAI -10.2% (z=-1.93). A steepener driven by term premium does not help banks; it marks their books.

The asymmetry is the whole page. SPX 7801.8 sits at the 98.8th percentile, +1.1% on the month, carried by QQQ/SPY at z=1.64, SOXX +12.2%, CIBR +12.7% (z=1.58, acc 1.60), AMD +35.2% and META +17.0%. Everything else is at the floor: RSP/SPY z=-2.13 at the 0th percentile, IWM/SPY 12th, XHB/SPY and IYT/SPY and EFA/SPY all 0th. Against that, VIX 15.77 at the 13th percentile (+4.6% today), VIX3M 17.72 at the 2.5th, SKEW -6.4% on the month with acceleration -1.85 — crash wings are being given away while MOVE still carries z=2.19. The one genuine bull argument is credit: HYG/IEF at the 97.5th percentile and +1.0% on the month, BKLN at the 93rd, credit composite +42. Own the carry, buy the insurance, stop owning the cyclical beta in between.

good.text: Credit still refuses to crack. HYG/IEF +1.0% on the month at the 97.5th percentile, BKLN at the 93rd, credit composite +42. This remains a discount-rate drawdown, not a default cycle — which is why the equity damage is relative, not absolute.
Bond volatility is deflating off the spike: MOVE -2.5% today and -7.1% on the week to 102.56, even with z still at 2.19. Cheaper carry for anyone wanting to own duration-sensitive steepeners.

The AI/semis engine is intact and leading: SOXX +12.2% on the month with +10.9% relative strength, CIBR +12.7% (z=1.58, acceleration 1.60), AMD +35.2% on the month, MU +281% ytd, META +17.0%. SMH/SPY z=1.14 and still accelerating.

Copper/gold made another 52-week high, +5.3% on the month at the 100th percentile, with copper +0.6% today. The metals unwind is monetary (gold -6.5%, silver -10.8% on the month), not a growth signal — growth pulse still +10.

Brazil is the one clean EM long: EWZ +11.9% on the month and +23.1% on three months, Bovespa z=1.74 at the 96th percentile, funded by USDBRL -2.3% on the month and -8.5% ytd while every other EM cross breaks the other way.
The 2-year is cooperating: -11bp on the week to 4.77%, pulling 2s10s +10bp on the month to 51bp with acceleration 0.60. A real front-end bid exists even as the long end is sold.

bad.text: The crude shock: WTI +4.4% and Brent +4.4% to 104.59, Brent +6.8% on the month, +37.1% on three months, +71.9% ytd, oil/gold +4.1% today. Gasoline -1.6% against it means refiners eat the first hit and the consumer eats the second.

Long-end and real yields keep accelerating against risk: 30-year 5.67% at the 100th percentile (acc 1.08), 10-year real 2.92% at z=1.92 with acceleration 1.38, 30-year mortgage 7.28% also 100th percentile. Rates composite -80.
Breadth is at the absolute floor and still falling: RSP/SPY z=-2.13, 0th percentile of 52 weeks, -4.6% on the month; IWM/SPY -7.0% on the month at the 12th percentile. The index is eight stocks wide.

The dollar re-accelerated rather than consolidated: DXY 102.4 at the 100th percentile with acceleration 1.66, EURUSD at the 0th percentile, USDCAD acc 1.84, USDMXN z=2.39/acc 1.90, USDINR acc 1.75. That is a tightening nobody voted for.

New crack: the financial complex. XLF -7.2% on the month (z=-1.66), KBE -8.8%, GS -14.6% (z=-2.08), BX -17.9% (z=-1.84), IAI -10.2% (z=-1.93, acc -1.50), KRE/SPY at the 13.8th percentile. Term-premium steepening is not bank-friendly steepening.
Ex-US equities rolled over on today's tape while US cash is stale: KOSPI -2.6%, Nikkei -1.4%, Hang Seng -1.4%, CAC -7.2% on the month at the 5th percentile, EFA/SPY z=-1.91 at the 0th percentile.

trades.name: Long XOP vs short SPY
trades.line: Long XOP vs SPY: crude +4.4%, energy equity hasn't marked it
trades.expr: Buy XOP, short equal-notional SPY. Cash-equity version: long XOM/CVX basket vs SPY. Avoid OIH — services are rolling over (-10.8% on the month, acc -1.29).
trades.thesis: Today's 4.4% move in both WTI and Brent happened after US energy equities last printed. Brent at 104.59 is +37.1% on three months with XLE's one-month relative strength at just -1.6% and XOP's at -2.0%. Equity has not discounted a $104 Brent; the three-month relative trends (XLE +9.7%, XOP +11.6%) say it eventually does.
trades.trigger: Brent +4.4% to 104.59 and WTI +4.4% to 92.16 on today's tape, Brent/WTI spread near $12.4, oil/gold +4.1% — all stamped 2026-10-08, while XOP/XLE/XOM are stamped 2026-10-07 and flat to down.
trades.stop: Brent closing back under $98, or XOP breaking 178 (-5%) on a day crude is higher.

trades.name: Own equity downside — vol is mispriced vs breadth
trades.line: Buy Dec SPY put spreads: VIX 13th pctile, breadth 0th
trades.expr: Buy December SPY 755/710 put spreads (roughly 3% and 9% below 777.22); alternatively November VIX 20/30 call spreads. Funded partly by selling 30-delta QQQ upside if you want the momentum long retained.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for the index, which is 0.5% from highs, while the actual portfolio under it is at 52-week relative lows. VIX 15.77 at the 13th percentile and VIX3M 17.72 at the 2.5th percentile against MOVE z=2.19 and a 10-year real yield at z=1.92 is a straight mispricing of the transmission from rates to stocks. SKEW -6.4% on the month with acceleration -1.85 means the wings are the cheap part.
trades.trigger: VIX +4.6% today with global cash down 1.0-2.6%, RSP/SPY at z=-2.13 and the 0th percentile, and a 4.4% crude shock the US market has not traded yet.
trades.stop: VIX3M sustained below 16 with RSP/SPY turning up and SPX making new highs on broadening participation; otherwise a hard time stop at December expiry.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener
trades.expr: Long 2-year notes (TU) versus duration-weighted short Ultra bond (WN). Unlevered version: short TLT against T-bills.
trades.thesis: This steepening is term premium, not easing, and term premium does not mean-revert quickly while the 30-year is accelerating (acc z=1.08) at the 100th percentile. The front end has already started to discount a slower economy — 2-year -11bp on the week — while the long end is being sold on supply and the oil shock. Falling MOVE makes the carry cheaper to hold.
trades.trigger: 30-year +3bp to 5.67% today, 10-year real 2.92% (z=1.92, acc 1.38), 2s10s +10bp on the month to 51bp and turning up, while MOVE fell 7.1% on the week to 102.56.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 35bp, or the 2-year back above 4.95% (front end repricing hawkish).

trades.name: Short housing (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.28% mortgage, 0th pctile, now an oil tax too
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy January ITB puts ~7% out of the money. Single-name version: short DHI, short HD.
trades.thesis: A 7.28% mortgage at the 100th percentile with the 10-year real yield still accelerating is not a sector that bottoms. ITB is -9.0% on the month at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks and XHB/SPY is -8.6% on the month at the 0th percentile — the trend is already confirmed, and a crude shock takes another slice of the same household budget.
trades.trigger: Mortgage 30-year 7.28%, +62bp on the month with z=1.85 and acceleration 1.27; ITB -2.6% and XHB -2.5% on Tuesday alone; HD -11.0% on the month at the 4.5th percentile; DHI -6.6%.
trades.stop: 10-year below 4.95% or the mortgage rate back under 7.00%; alternatively ITB reclaiming its 200-day (currently 12% above spot).

trades.name: Long EWZ / short INDA
trades.line: Long EWZ vs INDA: BRL strengthening, INR at z=1.79
trades.thesis: EM is no longer one asset class; it is a function of each currency's response to a 100th-percentile dollar. Brazil is the only major EM where the cross is working for you — USDBRL -2.3% on the month, -8.5% ytd — and the equity market is confirming with Bovespa z=1.74. India is the mirror image: USDINR +7.8% ytd with z=1.79 and acceleration 1.75, Sensex -16.0% ytd at the 0th percentile.
trades.trigger: EWZ +11.9% on the month with relative strength +17.8% on three months, versus INDA -7.6% on the month at the 7th percentile and -8.7% relative; USDINR +0.4% again today.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25, or the pair giving back 6% from entry.

trades.name: Short IAI vs long XLV
trades.line: Short IAI vs long XLV: capital markets crack, defensives bid
trades.expr: Short IAI (brokers/exchanges), long XLV equal-notional. More aggressive single-name expression: short BX versus long LLY.
trades.thesis: The capital-markets complex is where the long end is now biting hardest: fee pipelines, mark-to-market books and leveraged balance sheets all reprice to a 5.67% 30-year. Health care is the defensive that is actually bid, with its relative trend turning up, and it has no oil-cost or funding-cost exposure.
trades.trigger: IAI -10.2% on the month at z=-1.93 with acceleration -1.50; GS -14.6% (z=-2.08); BX -17.9% at the 20th percentile; XLF -7.2% on the month while SPX is +1.1%. XLV +1.0% on the day as the best sector, LLY +2.7%.
trades.stop: KBE reclaiming its 200-day, or the 30-year back below 5.35% with XLF recovering half its monthly loss.

trades.name: Long SMH / short IWM
trades.line: Long SMH vs IWM: ride narrowness while credit holds
trades.expr: Long SMH, short equal-notional IWM. Size small — SMH is 23.9% above its 200-day.
trades.thesis: Narrowness is not a bug to fade until funding cracks, and funding is fine: HYG/IEF is at the 97.5th percentile. Until credit spreads actually widen, the discount-rate shock keeps punishing the levered, domestic, small-cap tail and sparing cash-generative semis.
trades.trigger: SOXX +12.2% on the month with +10.9% relative strength and acceleration 1.01; AMD +35.2% on the month at z=1.73; versus IWM -5.9% on the month and IWM/SPY at z=-1.95, 12th percentile and still falling.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF breaking below its 200-day, or a 7% drawdown in the pair.
